supersedes.delta: +0.0474 strict F1, +0.0502 recall, for ~$0.88 and 43 extra minutes

stopping_rule.rule: TrainConfig.train_subsample: escalate only while BELOW ceiling AND train loss still falling
stopping_rule.evidence: val loss 0.01226 -> 0.01192 across the final epoch is a 2.8% move against 38% for epoch 1->2; train loss is 0.003. The curve has flattened, so more rows or epochs are not the binding constraint.
stopping_rule.remaining_gap: 0.9182 vs 0.9942 ceiling. Recall (0.8977) still trails precision (0.9397): 245 spans missed, 138 invented. If this is pursued, the next knob is LoRA rank (16), not data — a different experiment, and not obviously worth ~$1 at this margin.

notes: Relaxed 0.9472 vs strict 0.9182: a 0.029 gap, so most remaining errors are missed or spurious spans rather than boundary slips.
The ceiling is 0.9942, not 1.0, because values appearing more than once are assigned left-to-right (D22). 0.9182 is 92.4% of what is achievable on this scorer.
revision_note: main was briefly overwritten by a weaker 3K/2-epoch run; this revision is the 8K/3-epoch adapter these numbers describe. Pinning the revision, not the branch, is what F16's manifest requires.
